newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian PM urges parliament to speed up budget.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian PM urges parliament to speed up budget.

text.p: Bulgarian Prime Minister Ivan Kostov on Tuesday urged parliament to hold extra sessions to push through the state budget before the introduction of a fixed exchange rate regime on July 1.

Kostov told a news conference his ruling Union of Democratic Forces was pressing for extraordinary parliamentary sessions and would meet other parliamentary parties on Wednesday to seek their support.

"We expect the other forces represented in parliament to show cooperation and understanding on this vital issue, as the budget law is the most important for the introduction of the currency board on July 1," he said.
"It is obligatory that the laws needed to prepare the legislative base for launching the currency board be passed by the end of June."
The government completed the 1997 consolidated state budget draft on Friday and submitted it to parliament for approval, initially at committee level.

The currency board aims to stabilise the economy by banning central bank lending to the government and commercial banks and requiring levs in circulation to be fully covered by foreign exchange reserves at a rate of 1,000 to the mark. -- Sofia Newsroom +359 2 91188
